newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi receives $170 million tobacco payment.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi receives $170 million tobacco payment.

text.p: Mississippi received a $170 million payment from the tobacco industry Tuesday, making the state the first in the nation to be compensated by major cigarette makers for the cost of treating ailing smokers.

The office of State Attorney General Mike Moore, who in 1994 filed the first state lawsuit against the industry, said the sum would be held in escrow with a SunTrust Bank branch in Pascagoula, Miss., until state officials decided what to do with the money.
"This is a great day for the people of Mississippi. We have a great opportunity with this money to do some things," said assistant Attorney General Trey Bobinger.

The payment was part of a $3.36 billion 25-year settlement that Mississippi and the tobacco industry announced earlier this month. The figure is nearly four times larger than the $940 million state officials originally sought as compensation for Medicaid funds spent for smoking-related illnesses since the early 1960s.

Under the settlement, the state was expected to receive another $68 million next year and $76.5 million in 1999. Annual payments were to reach $136 million by the sixth year of the settlement and remain at that level.

Last month, Mississippi and 39 other states, which had followed its lead by suing tobacco companies, announced a $368.5 billion national settlement with the industry. Mississippi's settlement was designed to secure money for the state in the event that the national agreement failed to receive the required congressional approval.
